cities.d: The must-see capital has a gorgeous old town lined with gothic, renaissance, baroque and neoclassical buildings. The country's best museums, hotels and eating places are located here.

x.around: For an overview of the routes, see the Vilnius City Public Transport Map. There are some 90 standard bus routes (marked in blue; numbers mostly between 1 and 100), six express buses (in green; from 1G to 6G) and 14 trolleybuses (in red; between 1 and 20). The numbers overlap, but e.g. bus 3, express bus 3G and trolleybus 3 run entirely different routes. They run 05:30-23:00.

hidden.d: Vilnius University now has faculties across the city and beyond, but this is the baroque core of it, with the library, courtyards, observatory and Church of St Johns (plural: Šv Jono, the Baptist and the Evangelist).
Part of a Ukrainian Greek Catholic monastery, and mostly built in the early 17th century.
Small independent museum of city history.
Ames Room, Pepper's Ghost, holograms, all the staples are here. Children will love it.
A Russian Orthodox church. Not to be confused with the RC St Nicholas on Šv Mikalojaus.
Varnelis (1917-2020) was an abstract artist who mostly lived in the USA, returning to Vilnius in 1998. His house is now part of National Museum, displaying his studio and works.

Neo-renaissance mansion where Lithuania's Act of Independence was signed on 16 February 1918. It's now a branch of the National Museum depicting the story of Lithuania as a separate nation, in which independent spirit it makes…
This has a permanent display of Fluxus artwork plus other rotating exhibitions.

x.intro: Vilnius is the capital and largest city of Lithuania. It has a beautiful baroque Old Town, listed as a , and excellent tourist facilities in all price ranges. It stands on the River Neris in the southeast pocket of the country, the Dzūkija region, and in 2023 had a population of 629,000.

must.d: The first cathedral was built here in 1251, reverting to pagan worship in 1263. Fire destroyed a second in 1419, a third in 1530 and a fourth in 1610.
This is the Upper Castle of a complex of three built from the 13th century, much bashed about, and abandoned from the 16th.
The last survivor of the walled city's nine gates, various called Medininkai Gate as the street led south to that village, Sharp Gate, and now Gate of Dawn.
An 18th-century palace which is the seat of the President of Lithuania. Guided tours are available at weekends, and the palace is also open to the public on Open House days.

Small flamboyant church in Gothic style, built by 1500 and little altered since. There is a legend that when Napoleon's campaigns brought him to Vilnius, he declared that he'd like to lift the church on his palm and carry it back…
The first church from around 1500 was wooden and burned down, and its successor was wrecked in the 1650s in the war with Russia.

n.en: Church of Saints Peter and Paul
n.es: iglesia de San Pedro y San Pablo
n.it: chiesa di San Pietro e San Paolo

must.d: The 326.5 m high telecommunications tower was completed in 1980 and is visible from far and wide. You can ride the lift to the restaurant and observation deck.
The New Arsenal was established in the 18th century and mostly served as a barracks. It's now part of the National Museum displaying Lithuania's history and cultural heritage.

next.d: 30 km west has two castles amid scenic lakes.
35 km northwest was medieval capital of Lithuania, and is a for its ancient mounds.
100 km west is the second largest city, and mostly modern but with a small Old Town.

x.safe: If you are a person of colour, you may get weird looks or otherwise be looked down upon from the locals. ===Emergency numbers=== * * * *

cities.d: 28 km west of Vilnius, popular for its picture-perfect castle surrounded by a lake.

x.around: The town is small enough for everything to be reached on foot. Footbridges link town, Island Castle and nearby peninsulas.

hidden.d: This followed a similar timeline to the island castle, raised against the Teutonic Knights, converted to a residence (where the Grand Duke was murdered in 1440, just to keep up the tradition) then to a nobles' prison before…

x.intro: Trakai is a city in the Dzūkija region of Lithuania, 28 km west of the capital Vilnius. It's on the shores of Lake Galvė and its star attraction is the Island Castle - this and the Peninsula Castle are from the 14th century, when the capital moved here and was fortified against attack. In 2020 Trakai had a population of 4141.

must.d: This is the one in all the tourist brochures, a redbrick Gothic mirage suspended between blue sky and lake, a seat of the medieval Duchy of Lithuania and nowadays a national symbol.

This is within the kenesa (synagogue) of the local Karaite Jews. Theirs is a bizarre story played out over 800 years, none of which you will glean from this museum, even if it hadn't been closed since 2020.
Neoclassical mansion completed in 1895 in a lakeside farm estate. It's sometimes called Tyszkiewicz Palace for its owners, but that name also applies to their stately pile in Vilnius.

next.d: where you probably started.
or to Birštonas, Prienai and Marijampolė.

cities.d: The second largest city, has interwar modernist architecture and a compact old town. National sports events are staged here.

x.around: Some 43 bus and 15 trolleybus routes criss-cross the city, running from 05:00 to 23:00. Use e-tickets or buy a ticket on board (with coins or debit/credit card). A single e-ticket is €0.70 - always validate it when boarding. On board tickets cost €1.50. E-tickets can be used with a Žiogas card (available at newsstands or certain supermarkets in Kaunas) or with the Žiogas app, available on Android and iOS.

hidden.d: Grandiose neo-classical building of 1928. Primarily a commercial bank, it has a small exhibition of Lithuanian banknotes and coins of the First Republic, and occasionally hosts larger art installations.
Small church at the north end of Vytautus bridge built in 1682-83 in Baroque style.
Two km south on the former Darius & Girėnas Airport, which now only has light aviation. The indoor exhibits (such as the flight simulator) closed during covid and have yet to re-open.
By appointment only.

Skansen-type outdoor ethnography museum on lake shore, with traditional buildings brought from around the country. In winter their interiors are closed up but you can still stroll around the park. Dogs permitted on leash outdoors.
The house was built in 1932 for soprano Adelė Nezabitauskaitė-Galaunienė (1895–1962) and art historian Paulius Galaunė (1890–1988). The architect was Arnas Funkas (1898–1957).

Antanas Žmuidzinavičius (1876-1966) was a distinguished landscape painter but now is better known for his huge collection of sculptures of devils. Some 3000 of them are here, from around the world but mainly central European.
Grandiose chunk of interbellum architecture, built at huge cost in 1937. Part of the "Modernist Kaunas: Architecture of Optimism, 1919–1939" UNESCO World Heritage Site.

x.intro: Kaunas at the edge of Sūduva region is the second-largest city in Lithuania, with a population of 304,000 in 2024. The main reason to visit is its Old Town, connected to the 19th-century New Town along Laisvės alėja. It was the country's capital between the two world wars.

must.d: The first castle was built mid-14th century at the confluence of the rivers Nemunas and Neris. It was destroyed in 1401 and the new castle was constructed in the 15th and 16th centuries. It is the oldest building in Kaunas.
This is first documented in 1413, in the reign of Vytautas the Great, but construction dragged on to 1624, nicely in time to get smashed up by the Russians and Swedes.

n.es: Catedral Basílica de San Pedro y San Pablo
n.it: cattedrale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo

must.d: Kaunas Fortress was a military defensive complex encircling the city, with ten forts built by the Russians 1882-1915 to protect their empire from the growing power of Germany.
Within Ąžuolynas Park, this was renovated in 2023 and now offers a better experience for animals and visitors.
Built from the 17th century as a Camaldolese monastery, this is a riot of Baroque thanks to its Italian architects and sculptors.
Gothic redbrick church built in 1400 for the Franciscan monks. It's suffered repeatedly from river floods, occupying armies and religious upheavals, but since 1919 has been Roman Catholic.

This beautiful domed building closes off the prospect down Laisvės Aleja. Opened in 1895, it was built in neo-Byzantine style for Russian soldiers based here, and to remind the townsfolk who was in charge.

n.en: Church of St Michael the Archangel

must.d: The Art Deco main branch of the museum was built in the 1930s and is next to the war museum. It showcases Lithuania's cultural heritage and especially the works of M K Čiurlionis (1875–1911), whose style ranged over symbolism,…

n.en: M K Čiurlionis Museum of Art
n.es: Museo Nacional de Arte Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis

next.d: is a must-see for its elegant old town. It can be done as a day-trip from Kaunas but deserves several days to explore.
is a spa resort 30 km south of Kaunas, set on a forested riverside.
is a spa town 50 km south, near the border with Belarus.

x.safe: Usual precautions about traffic, safeguarding valuables and avoiding damnfool drunks.

cities.d: The country's only port, so much is industrial, but with a distinctive half-timbered old town. Popular for its annual Sea Festival.

x.around: A single paper ticket costs €0.80 from a kiosk and €1 from the bus driver. Validate your ticket immediately on boarding.

hidden.d: The most substantial of the World War II fortifications dotted along the spit. This group of overgrown ruins was Schweinsrücken artillery battery.
Sūduvis was a West German minesweeper, in service from 1958. It was handed over to Lithuania in 1999 and retired in 2021.
This annex of the Sea Museum is a Skansen-type outdoor museum of fishermen's cottages and equipment.
The 19th century breakwater at the very tip of the spit, reached by a paved track.

x.intro: Klaipėda is a city in Lithuania Minor, the narrow northwest coastal region of Lithuania. It's the country's third-largest city. The city has historic sights but isn't pretty-pretty like Vilnius Old Town, and draws mostly local tourism. The big attraction is the Curonian Spit, a remarkable 99 km peninsula of sand dunes. Smiltynė at its north tip is part of the city and is reached by a five-minute ferry ride from downtown.

must.d: It contains more than 80 wooden statues of Lithuanian folklore characters.
Displays of marine life plus maritime history. You pay as much again for the dolphin shows in the Dolphinarium.

next.d: on the Curonian Spit is reached by ferry to Smiltynė then by road. Between Smiltynė and Nida is Juodkrantė, which can make for a nice day trip.
is a lively beach resort north towards the border with Latvia.
is Lithuanian's charming capital, with a well-preserved baroque centre.

x.safe: Klaipėda is a safe place but like anywhere you have to use common sense. Try to walk with a confident air and not look lost.

cities.d: Several museums, sculptures and old churches can be found here, but it's best known for the "Hill of Crosses" 12 km north.

x.around: Walk: The city sprawls, but most points of interest are within a compact area.

hidden.d: Models and sculptures of angels - cute, moving or emetic as the mood takes you.
Small but well-maintained by the university.
Rebuilt in 2022, the city's history is now exhibited here.
A 19th century windmill restored to working order.
Small exhibition of what your gran watched, no signage in English.
The town has a bicycle factory Baltik vairas, and this quirky museum exhibits the history of the bike.
Small museum on the history of photography, but short on actual photos.
Collection of feline memorabilia, plus six live cats that appreciate being stroked, and a sad mini-zoo.

x.intro: Šiauliai (show-LAY) is an industrial city in Samogitia, the northwest region of Lithuania, though it borders Aukštaitija the northeast region. It's the country's fourth largest city: in 2023 the population was 40,434, with a total of about 108,000 across the metropolis. It's a modern city with several sites of interest, but the stand-out is the "Hill of Crosses" pilgrimage site 12 km north.

must.d: Prominent with its 75 m spire, this large Roman Catholic church was built in Renaissance style in the 1620s. It was part defensive - note the shooting loops - as it was at risk from armed robbery and sectarian riots.

n.es: Catedral de San Pedro y San Pablo
n.it: cattedrale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo

next.d: Lithuania's third largest city, lies west. It's modern but with many points of interest, and a short ferry-ride brings you to the Curonian Spit.
is a beach resort north of Klaipėda.
Lithuania's second city, is southeast, with many features of its time as a Russian bastion then a Polish city.
north in Latvia has a fascinating old town centre.

cities.d: Drably industrial, but has museums, churches and a heritage narrow-gauge railway.

x.around: Most sights are within walking distance of the centre. Stops-Lt displays city bus routes: Bus 6A runs hourly from Janonio g and the railway station downtown then east out to Dembava.

hidden.d: This 1960s Soviet military base has been turned into an outdoor amusement park with picnic areas, sculpture park and scary bunkers.
This stretches west of town along the south river bank, with cycling trails and fishing spots. Dogs welcome.
Museum of natural history, city history and culture, founded in 1925 and on its present site in the Moigių mansion since 1985.

This was intended as the site of a cathedral, never needed for that, so it opened as a cemetery in 1914. The First World War rapidly filled its plots but it's still in use, a bosky resting place for the city's great and good.
Larger wooded park east of the river loop.
Planned from 1860 but with construction delayed by war and hostile authorities, this Roman Catholic cathedral was eventually consecrated in 1933. The style is a mix of Baroque and Neoclassical.
Roman Catholic church completed in 1885, in Neo-Renaissance red brick.
This was completed in 1885 but looks older, a traditional Gothic wooden church in light paint.

x.intro: Panevėžys is an industrial city in the Aukštaitija region of Lithuania. It's the country's fifth largest city, with a population of 89,100 in 2021 and another 30,000 or so in the city district. It's about midway along the highway between Vilnius the capital and Riga the Latvian capital.

next.d: to the west is best known for the Hill of Crosses.
beach resort and Klaipėda city.
is mostly modern, but with an old centre and wartime fortifications.
has a charming town centre in Baroque style.
the capital of Latvia has a great mix of ancient, Soviet and modern.

cities.d: Generally only of interest to refrigerator manufacturers, but is a base for exploring the Dzūkija National Park further south.

x.around: Town centre is walkable but you need wheels for outlying sights.
x.intro: Alytus is a city in Dzūkija or Dainava Region of southern Lithuania. It has an old core but is mostly modern and industrial, and you'd probably only visit if you were in the refrigerator business. In 2023 Alytus had a population of 53,514.

next.d: 22 km east is a lakeside resort.
the capital is a must-see for its baroque architecture.
the medieval capital has a scenic island castle.
is mostly modern but has an old centre and the bastions of its wartime defences.

intro: Lithuania (Lithuanian: Lietuva) is one of the three Baltic states of northeast Europe. It's a low-lying, mostly agricultural country bordered by Latvia to the north and east, Belarus to the south, Poland to the southwest, Kaliningrad exclave of Russia to the west, and the Baltic Sea to the northwest. It broke away from the Soviet Union to become an independent republic in 1990, soon followed by Latvia and Estonia, the other two Baltic states.

other.d: is a 99 km strip of sand dunes, forest and secluded villages.

x.around: It's easy to explore either end of the spit by car or bicycle, and each country has a bus service.
x.intro: The Curonian Spit is a sandy peninsula in the Baltic Sea, 99 km long but only 0.5 to 4 km wide. Its northern part is in Lithuania Minor and its south in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad Oblast: both countries regard it as a national park and it's a bi-national UNESCO World Heritage Site.

other.d: is a pilgrimage site with a large church festival in July.

hidden.d: This is the principle church, built in Baroque-cum-Neoclassical from 1780, and restored after various calamities.

n.en: Basilica of the Visitation of the Virgin Mary

x.intro: Žemaičių Kalvarija meaning Samogitian Calvary is a village in the Samogitia region of Lithuania, 25 km northeast of the provincial chief town of Plungė. It's a Roman Catholic pilgrimage destination and in 2021 had a population of 600.

next.d: 80 km west is the main beach resort in Lithuania, and has the regional airport.
30 km south of Palanga is a city with several antiquities.
a short ferry ride from Klaipėda, is a 99 km bootlace of sandhills and forest.
in Latvia is 80 km northwest of Žemaičių Kalvarija. It's a large beach resort with a scenic ruined fortress, a cathedral, and mementoes of its Soviet past.

other.d: was the capital in medieval times, now an archaeological site.

x.around: You need your own car to see much of this region. Highways radiate from Vilnius and are in good condition, well-signposted and toll-free. Winter driving can be challenging.
x.intro: Dzūkija or Dainava is one of the five "cultural regions" of Lithuania, in the south of the country bordering Belarus. This region is ill-defined, so on these pages it's taken as Vilnius city and county plus Alytus county.

next.d: to the west is the main city of Sūduva region bordering Poland.
. Buses and trains run further north via Kaunas and Marijampolė towards Suwałki.
